passes.note: F1 verified resolved by simulation (1 px shift 2.12 %, 10 % darker 97.4 %).

findings.area: gate honesty / spec fidelity (FR-EDT-010, parity metric)
findings.detail: The parity metric excused any differing pixel on an edge in both images, so a 1 px displacement of all content, or a text anti-aliasing change, scored 0 %.
findings.failure_scenario: A chrome change shifts edit content by 1 px or changes its font smoothing; the content DOM is identical, diffPct reports ~0 %, and FR-EDT-010 breaks unseen.
findings.resolution: M6.34 (42ea954, 30ec085): pixelmatch's anti-aliasing test with a brightness-spread condition (PARITY_EDGE_DELTA); the spec asserts the screen darkened by 10 % and moved 1 px right and down all score over the bound. Pass 2 verified by simulation: a 1 px shift scores ~2.1 % against 0.1 %.

findings.detail: Parity compares only the first screens of the two examples; the editor cannot show other screens or open files yet.
findings.failure_scenario: Once later screens and files open in edit, a screen that draws differently in edit never enters the suite.

findings.detail: F5 and shift+F5 are the same switch (always the editor's first screen), and present in place does not drive the player's PresentationController.
findings.failure_scenario: After M8 a user presses shift+F5 on screen 3 and presents screen 1; after M11 arrows navigate in /present but not in F5 in place.

findings.area: gate honesty over time (NFR-PERF-001: perf.drag-500, hit-test-2000)
findings.detail: The drag benchmark and the hit-test bench run only in m6-complete; no later gate or CI job reruns them; only a drag (not a resize) is measured; the spec's 'a second' comment disagrees with its 30-frame floor.
findings.failure_scenario: M7 or M19 slows the hit index or drag rendering and no gate notices until M32.

findings.detail: cp1 F7 was argued without a line in review-argued.txt; the checkpoint records spell 'hand off' where the gate's enum is 'hand-off'.
findings.failure_scenario: The final record copies 'hand off' and the final-review leg refuses it; a later reviewer finds no trace of the cp1 F7 argument.

findings.detail: The stricter metric also flags a text anti-aliasing mode change (LCD vs grayscale, e.g. a compositing layer on the edit canvas): ~1.1 % on text screens.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change composites the edit canvas and parity turns red although nothing is wrong to the eye; correct under FR-EDT-010's pixel-identical wording.
